chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said: Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) sent to me the will of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and it is:

In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. This is what Abd Allah Ali bequeathed and decreed regarding his wealth, seeking the Face of Allah, so that He may admit me into Paradise by it, and turn me away from the Fire by it, and turn the Fire away from me on the Day when faces become white and faces become black.

That which was mine of wealth in Yanbu', known to me therein and what is around it, is charity, along with its slaves, except that Rabah, Abu Nayzar, and Jubayr are emancipated, there is no way for anyone over them, so they are my mawali, who work in the property for five years (hijj), and in it is their expenses and their livelihood, and the livelihoods of their families.

And with that, all that was mine of wealth in Wadi al-Qura is for the children of Fatima, and its slaves are charity. And what was mine in Dayma and its people is charity, except that Zureeq has what I wrote for his companions. And what was mine in Udhaynah and its people is charity, and the two poor ones, as you know, are charity in the way of Allah.

And that which I wrote from this wealth of mine is an obligatory, final charity, whether I am alive or dead. It is spent in every expenditure sought by which is the Face of Allah, in the way of Allah and His Face, and the relatives from the children of Hashim and the children of al-Muttalib, and the near and the far. For al-Hasan ibn Ali will oversee that, consuming from it with goodness and spending it wherever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sees fit, in a permissible manner, with no hardship upon him in it.
So if he wishes to sell a share of the property to pay off a debt, let him do so if he wishes, and there is no hardship upon him in it. And if he wishes, he can make it a series of properties (waqf).

And the children of Ali, their mawali, and their wealth are to al-Hasan ibn Ali. And if the house of al-Hasan ibn Ali is other than the house of charity, and it seems to him that he should sell it, let him sell if he wishes, with no hardship upon him in it. And if he sells, he divides its price into three thirds: he makes one third in the way of Allah, one third among the children of Hashim and the children of al-Muttalib, and he makes the third among the family of Abu Talib, and he places it among them wherever Allah sees fit.

And if a thing befalls Hasan (i.e., he dies) and Husayn is alive, then it is to Husayn ibn Ali. And Husayn will do with it what I ordered Hasan to do; he has what I wrote for Hasan, and upon him is what was upon Hasan.

And for the children [sons] of Fatima from the charity of Ali is what is for the children of Ali. And I only made what I made for the sons of Fatima seeking the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and honoring the sanctity of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and exalting them, and honoring them, and seeking their pleasure.

And if a thing befalls Hasan and Husayn, then the last of the two looks among the children of Ali. If he finds among them one whom he is pleased with in his guidance, his Islam, and his trustworthiness, he makes it to him if he wishes. And if he does not see in them all that he wants, he makes it to a man from the family of Abu Talib whom he is pleased with.

If he finds that the family of Abu Talib has lost their elders and those of insight, he makes it to a man whom he is pleased with from the children of Hashim. And he stipulates upon the one to whom he makes it that he leaves the wealth upon its origins and spends its fruits wherever I ordered from the way of Allah and His Face, and the relatives from the children of Hashim and the children of al-Muttalib, and the near and the far. Nothing from it is sold, nor gifted, nor inherited.
And the wealth of Muhammad ibn Ali is on its side, and it is to the two sons of Fatima. And my slaves who are in the small parchment that was written for me are emancipated.

This is what Ali ibn Abi Talib decreed regarding this wealth of his, the morning of the day he arrived at Maskan, seeking the Face of Allah and the Last Home. And Allah is the One sought for help in every situation. And it is not permissible for a Muslim man who believes in Allah and the Last Day to say about anything I have decreed from my wealth, nor to contradict my order in it, from the near or the far.

As for what follows, my slave-wives, upon whom I circle, are seventeen of them. From them are mothers of children, with them their children, and from them are pregnant, and from them is one who has no child. So my decree regarding them is that if a thing befalls me, whoever of them has no child and is not pregnant, she is free for the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there is no way for anyone over them. And whoever of them has a child or is pregnant, she is kept for her child, and she is from his share. If her child dies and she is alive, she is free, there is no way for anyone over her.
This is what Ali decreed regarding his wealth, the morning of the day he arrived at Maskan. Witnessed by Abu Shimr ibn Abraha, and Sa'sa'ah ibn Suhan, and Yazid ibn Qays, and Hayyaj ibn Abi Hayyaj.
And Ali ibn Abi Talib wrote with his own hand, for the ten days remaining from Jumada al-Ula, the year thirty-seven. And the second will was with the first.

In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. This is what Ali ibn Abi Talib bequeathed, bequeathing that he testifies that there is no god except Allah, One, without a partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, whom He sent with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion, even if the polytheists dislike it. Peace be upon him and his family. Then, indeed, my prayer and my sacrifice and my life and my death are for Allah, Lord of the worlds, without a partner. And with that I was commanded, and I am of the Muslims.

Then I bequeath to you, O Hasan, and all my family and my children, and whoever reaches my letter, to fear Allah, your Lord. And do not die except while you are Muslims. And hold fast to the rope of Allah all together and do not separate. For I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: 'Reconciliation is better than the majority of prayer and fasting.' And the destroyer, the hair-shaver of the religion, is discord. And there is no strength except with Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent.
Look to your relatives and maintain ties with them, Allah will make the Reckoning easy for you.

Allah, Allah regarding the orphans, so do not delay their mouths (feeding them) and do not let them perish in your presence. For I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: 'Whoever supports an orphan until he becomes independent, Allah obligates for him Paradise by that, just as He obligated for the consumer of the orphan's wealth the Fire.'

Allah, Allah regarding the Quran, so no one precedes you to acting upon it. Allah, Allah regarding your neighbors, for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) bequeathed them, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not cease to bequeath them until we thought he would make them inheritors.

Allah, Allah regarding the House of your Lord, so do not let it be empty of you as long as you remain. For if it is left, you will not be questioned. And the least of what one returns with from his mother is that what is past is forgiven for him.

Allah, Allah regarding the Prayer, for it is the best of deeds, indeed it is the pillar of your religion. Allah, Allah regarding Zakat, for it extinguishes the wrath of your Lord. Allah, Allah regarding the month of Ramadan, for its fasting is a shield from the Fire. Allah, Allah regarding the poor and the needy, so share them in your livelihoods.
Allah, Allah regarding Jihad with your wealth, your selves, and your tongues. Indeed, two men perform Jihad: an Imam of Guidance, or one obedient to him, following his guidance.
Allah, Allah regarding the offspring of your Prophet, so they should not be oppressed in your presence or between your sides, while you have the ability to defend them.

Allah, Allah regarding the companions of your Prophet who did not innovate anything new and did not harbor an innovator. For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) bequeathed them and cursed the innovator from them and from others, and the one who harbors the innovator.

Allah, Allah regarding the women and what your right hands possess, for the last of what your Prophet (peace be upon him) spoke was that he said: 'I bequeath you with the two weak ones: the women and what your right hands possess.'

Prayer, Prayer, Prayer. Do not fear in Allah the blame of a blamer. Allah will suffice you against those who harm you and act arrogantly against you. Speak good to people as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded you. And do not leave enjoining good and forbidding evil, lest Allah make your rulers the worst of you, then you call out and your call is not answered against them.

And upon you, O my sons, is maintaining ties, generosity, and excellence. Beware of cutting off, aversion, and separation. And cooperate in righteousness and piety, and do not cooperate in sin and aggression. And fear Allah, indeed Allah is Severe in retribution.
May Allah protect you from a family, and protected among you is your Prophet. I entrust you to Allah, and convey to you greetings, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.

Then he did not cease saying 'La ilaha illa Allah, La ilaha illa Allah' until he was taken (died). May the prayers of Allah and His mercy be upon him, during the three nights from the last ten, the night of twenty-three from the month of Ramadan, the night of Friday, the year forty from the Hijra. And he was struck on the night of twenty-one from the month of Ramadan.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific bequests and financial rulings detailed in the will of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith provides the primary textual evidence for the concept of *Waqf* (endowment) in Shia jurisprudence, detailing Imam Ali’s (as) strategic distribution of wealth to preserve the status of the Ahl al-Bayt. The document not only outlines the legal transfer of assets to Hasan and Husayn but also emphasizes the spiritual imperative of maintaining family ties (*Silat al-Rahim*) and supporting the poor, reflecting the practical application of Quranic injunctions on charity. This will serves as a foundational model for Shia inheritance law, distinguishing between inheritable property and perpetual endowments dedicated to the Prophet’s lineage.
